info.title: STS REST API v1
info.description: Shipper-Driven Traffic Simulator API. All v1 fields are snake_case. Success responses are `{"data": ..., "meta": {...}}`; errors are `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`. Authentication is a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer sts_...`) with hierarchical roles reader < operator < editor < admin. GETs are open unless the server sets `STS_API_READ_OPEN=0`. Each operation states its minimum role in `x-sts-role`. Tokens are managed under `/admin/tokens` or with `php sts/api/bin/tokens.php`. Cross-site writes are rejected: a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE that carries an `Origin` header whose host:port differs from the request `Host` gets 403 (requests without `Origin`, such as curl, RFID devices and helpers, are unaffected). `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is sent for GET/HEAD only; for writes it is echoed only for a same-host origin. Maintenance lock: while an exclusive task (restore, warm start, begin, play, workflow run or a destructive command) is queued or running, every other write route answers 409 `maintenance task <id> running`; reads, `/admin/tokens` and `POST /admin/tasks/{id}/fail` are not blocked. Reads under `STS_API_READ_OPEN=1` (the default) need no token, which includes `/settings`, `/backups` and `/sessions`; only `/tasks` always needs the `operator` role. A browser can sign in with `POST /auth/login` and then authenticate with the `sts_api` session cookie (`cookieAuth`); revoking the underlying token ends its sessions. Command roles and the open flags come from the policy (`/admin/policy`), not only the environment.

bearerAuth.description: Token of the form sts_ followed by 40 hex characters.

cookieAuth.name: sts_api
cookieAuth.description: Browser session cookie set by POST /auth/login (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/sts/, 12 hour idle timeout). It stands in for a bearer token; the underlying token is rechecked on every request.

Forbidden.description: Token role too low, destructive recipe without admin, or a cross-site write (403 forbidden).

Maintenance.description: A maintenance (exclusive) task is queued or running; writes wait (409 conflict, `maintenance task <id> running`).
